n01.Mean of four readings: The array method `.mean()` returns a float already — no loop, no manual division.
n01.How many above one: Compare the array with 1 to get a boolean mask, then `.sum()` counts the True values.
n01.Gap between largest and smallest: `.max()` and `.min()` each return one value; subtract them and keep it an int.
n01.ints become floats on request: Either pass `dtype=float` when building, or call `.astype(float)` afterwards.
n01.Text keeps its values: `.tolist()` returns plain Python strings, not NumPy scalars.
n01.Shape of a nested list: `.shape` is a tuple of axis lengths — store it unchanged.
n01.Read the last value: A negative index counts from the end: `-1` is the last element.
n01.Squares of a range: Square the whole array with `** 2`, then convert with `.tolist()`.
n01.Product of three values: `.prod()` multiplies every element; wrap the result in `int()`.
n01.Sum of squares: Square the array first, then reduce with `.sum()`.
n01.Subtract two vectors: Array minus array pairs positions; convert the result with `.tolist()`.
n01.Halve a range: Divide the array by 2 — the result is float, so `.tolist()` gives 0.0, 0.5, …
n01.Count every element: `.size` counts all cells; `.shape` would count per axis instead.
n01.Repeat a value four times: `np.full(4, 3)` writes one value into four cells.
n01.Element-wise product of two vectors: `*` multiplies position by position; `@` would be matrix multiplication.
n01.Booleans add up: A boolean array stores True as 1, so `.sum()` counts them.
n01.Smallest of a small grid: `.min()` reduces every axis by default, whatever the shape.
n01.Reciprocals of one and two: Divide 1 by the array; the result is float, then `.tolist()`.
n01.Distance between two numbers: `np.abs(3 - 8)` keeps the sign out of the answer; store an int.
n01.Two arrays are equal: `np.array_equal(a, b)` returns a single bool, unlike `==` which returns a mask.
n01.Axes of a two-row grid: `.ndim` reports how many axes an array has.
n01.Double, then take the first two: Multiply the array, then slice `[:2]`; `.tolist()` at the end.
n01.Count the values above ten: Build the mask with `> 10`, then count with `.sum()`.
